title: Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) Training Notes: Compounding of Pass-Through Rows Elected for Early Retirement
content:
# Compounding of Pass-Through Rows Elected for Early Retirement

*Training notes — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).*

**The rule.** For a wholesale-supplier pass-through row a former member elects under an approved discounted early retirement, the pass-through discount is compounded by the size of the row's gross: a gross under **$100.00** is compounded monthly at one twelfth of the rate; a gross of at least $100.00 and under **$250.00** is compounded twice a year at one half of the rate; a gross of at least $250.00 is compounded once a year.

## Questions answered

**What is the gross?** The pass-through amount of that allocation year as booked, less every general retirement already booked on it, rounded to the cent.

**What does monthly compounding mean in figures?** One plus one twelfth of the rate, as a decimal, is raised to the power of twelve times the horizon in years, and the gross is divided by the result.

**And twice a year?** One plus one half of the rate is raised to the power of two times the horizon in years.

**And once a year?** One plus the rate is raised to the power of the horizon in years.

**Is a gross of exactly $100.00 compounded monthly?** No. $100.00 is "at least $100.00", so it is compounded twice a year. A gross of exactly $250.00 is compounded once a year.

## Worked figures (hypothetical rate of 9 percent and horizon of 5 years)

| Gross | Compounding | Divisor | Discounted value |
|---|---|---|---|
| $60.00 | monthly | 1.0075 raised to the power 60, which is 1.565681 | $38.32 |
| $150.00 | twice a year | 1.045 raised to the power 10, which is 1.552969 | $96.59 |
| $400.00 | once a year | 1.09 raised to the power 5, which is 1.538624 | $259.97 |
